title: Going from Place to Place
editorial: Flights do most of the heavy lifting, but you’ll need your driver’s license for Patagonia.

Santiago to Rapa Nui is a long haul at 6+ hours, but it’s by far the most luxurious domestic flight we’ve taken in South America. There’s a special gate at the airport for Rapa Nui flights, so be sure to reach early in case you have trouble locating it.

To get to Patagonia, you’ll need to fly from Santiago to Puerto Natales and rent a car to ride about an hour to Torres del Paine National Park. One important thing to note… there were no gas stations / petrol pumps inside the park, so be sure to purchase extra cans of fuel.

To go further south to Punta Arenas, you can catch a 3-hour bus from Puerto Natales. There were no international flights out of Puerto Natales, so you’ll be headed back to Santiago to check out of Chile.
